rationale: The literature confirms that seizures and epilepsy (HP:0001250) are a cardinal and recurrent manifestation of biallelic GTF3C3-related neurodevelopmental disorder (OMIM #621201). However, the reported frequency varies substantially across cohorts. While early reports and cohort descriptions identified seizures in approximately 75% of individuals (e.g., 9 affected individuals reported in early plenary data and described across 12 individuals in De Hayr et al.), detailed cohort phenotyping by Abdel-Hamid et al. identified seizures in only half of their patients (2 of 4 individuals, 50%). Therefore, the estimated frequency range of 70–90% is an overestimation in some cohorts, demonstrating incomplete penetrance of epilepsy in GTF3C3 deficiency.

evidence.text: In a cohort of four individuals from three unrelated families harboring biallelic GTF3C3 variants, seizures were only documented in 50% of the individuals, demonstrating that epilepsy is not present in a 70-90% majority in all cohorts.

source.title: Biallelic variants in GTF3C3 encoding a subunit of the TFIIIC2 complex are associated with neurodevelopmental phenotypes in humans and zebrafish
source.quote: Seizures were observed in half of the patients. Exome/genome sequencing revealed four different GTF3C3 variants including three missense (p.Cys172Gly, p.Val427Phe and p.Ala509Thr) and one nonsense variant (p.Arg717Ter).

evidence.text: Characterization of a cohort of 12 individuals from 7 unrelated families with biallelic GTF3C3 missense variants confirmed seizures alongside intellectual disability, motor impairments, and brain anomalies.

source.title: Biallelic variants in GTF3C3 result in an autosomal recessive disorder with intellectual disability
source.quote: Twelve affected individuals from 7 unrelated families were identified with homozygous or compound heterozygous missense variants in GTF3C3... The cohort presented with intellectual disability, variable nonfamilial facial features, motor impairments, seizures, and cerebellar/corpus callosum malformations.

evidence.text: An opening plenary session presenting the initial multi-individual GTF3C3 disease cohort documented seizures in 9 affected individuals.

source.title: Plenary Sessions Pl1 Opening Plenary
source.quote: The cohort manifests a core neurodevelopmental phenotype... and congenital anomalies, and seizures in nine individuals.

evidence.text: GTF3C3 was identified as a candidate gene for early-onset epileptic encephalopathies in affected siblings presenting with seizures, mild intellectual disability, and dysmorphisms.

source.title: The role of recessive inheritance in early-onset epileptic encephalopathies: a combined whole-exome sequencing and copy number study

conflicts: Abdel-Hamid et al. (2025) reported seizures in exactly 2 of 4 (50%) individuals with biallelic GTF3C3 variants, contradicting the hypothesis that seizures are present in 70-90% of all affected patients.

While cohorts ascertained via epileptic encephalopathy pipelines present seizures in high proportions (e.g., 9 individuals in the plenary cohort), broader neurodevelopmental cohorts show variable penetrance of epilepsy.

new_directions.question_text: Does the presence and severity/refractoriness of seizures in GTF3C3-related disorder correlate with specific variant types (e.g., truncating vs. missense) or the degree of RNA polymerase III transcription impairment?
new_directions.rationale: Differences in seizure penetrance between cohorts (50% vs ~75%) may stem from hypomorphic missense variants retaining partial Pol III regulatory activity versus null/truncating variants.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true lifetime penetrance of epilepsy in GTF3C3 disorder when longitudinal follow-up beyond early childhood is assessed across all international registries?
new_directions.rationale: Patients documented without seizures in early evaluations (such as in Abdel-Hamid et al.) may develop seizures at a later age, which would clarify whether penetrance eventually reaches 70-90%.
